narrative.question: You wrote a skill and it works when you try it. Does it work?
narrative.viewer_starts: Has written or used a skill for a coding agent, and has not evaluated one.

arc.viewer_can: say what problem the course starts from and who it is for
name the seven parts and where they lead

scenes.on_screen: The course name in the display serif, under the eyebrow 'A course in seven parts'. Below: 'It works when you try it. Does it work?'
narration: You wrote a skill for a coding agent, and it works when you try it.
But you can't tell whether it works on another model, on the fifth run, or after your next edit, or what each run costs.
This course is for anyone who writes skills, or builds an agent into an app, and wants evidence in place of a hunch.

scenes.on_screen: Headline 'One skill, measured'. Seven blocks in two rows, one named for each part of the course.
narration: We take one short skill, which writes changelog entries, and measure it with Vally.
First we measure the skill, and read what the agent really did.
Then we build graders we can trust, and ask whether the skill earns its place.
We add a judge for what code can't check, and learn what a result does and doesn't support.
We work out what a passing trial costs, and turn the checks into a routine.
Finally, we evaluate the same skill inside an app.

scenes.on_screen: 'Say it with evidence' in the display serif. Below: 'Did the change make it better, and what does it cost?'
narration: By the end, you can change the skill, or the model under it, and say with evidence whether it got better, and what it costs.
